mood.headline: Flat-to-weak open likely: GIFT Nifty flat at 22,595, but $115 Brent and Infosys's guidance cut weigh.
mood.summary: GIFT Nifty was at 22,595 (−13, −0.06%) at 7:23 AM after recovering from an early low of 22,533, pointing to a flat start near Friday's 22,600 close. The pressure is oil: Brent settled at $116.72 on Friday (+3.1%, a six-month high) and is $115.48 early Monday after Houthi missile attacks on Saudi Arabia and Trump saying a new Iran strike is possible. Asia is mildly lower (Nikkei −0.9%, Kospi −0.2% at the open) after a weak Friday on Wall Street (Dow −1.23%). Infosys cut its FY27 growth guidance to 1–2%, which can weigh on IT, while Kotak, IDFC First, AU SFB, Coforge and JSW Steel reported strong numbers. Nifty must hold 22,372 (Friday's low) and 22,180–22,220; 22,835–22,850 is the first hurdle ahead of Tuesday's expiry and the Fed decision late Wednesday IST.

brief.text: Expect a flat start: GIFT Nifty is at 22,595 (−0.06%) against Friday's Nifty close of 22,600; support is 22,372 and then 22,180–22,220, resistance 22,835–22,850.
Oil is the main worry: Brent settled at $116.72 on Friday, a six-month high, and is $115.48 this morning after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Trump saying an Iran strike is possible.
Infosys cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1–2% from 1.5–3%; its US-listed shares were down about 6% before the US open Friday, so IT may open weak.
Banks reported well over the weekend: Kotak profit +26% to ₹5,645 cr, IDFC First nearly tripled to ₹1,045 cr, AU SFB +53%; FIIs bought ₹888 cr and DIIs ₹3,235 cr on Friday.

news.headline: GIFT Nifty flat near 22,595 after early dip
news.summary: GIFT Nifty was at 22,595, down 13 points, after recovering from an early low of 22,533.5. Brent was above $115 and Asian markets were mixed to weak.
news.why: Points to a flat start near 22,600; Friday's 22,372 low is the line that matters.

news.headline: Brent hits six-month high of $116.72; eases to $115.48 Monday
news.summary: Brent rose 3.1% on Friday and 6.2% for the week on Saudi attacks and US–Israel strike talk, then slipped 1% early Monday. WTI is at $102.08.
news.why: Costly oil hurts the rupee, inflation and margins of oil marketing companies, paints, airlines and tyre makers.

news.headline: Trump: no Iran strike Sunday, but 'a possibility'; Houthis fire missiles at Saudi Arabia
news.summary: Saudi-led forces intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh and 10 more at the south on 25 Oct; debris hurt two people. Trump said there would be no strike that day but later said he might act, while also mentioning a possible deal.
news.why: Keeps the oil risk premium high; any actual strike would hit Indian stocks and the rupee and lift gold.

news.headline: Infosys cuts FY27 growth guidance to 1–2% despite $5.2 bn deals
news.summary: Q2 profit rose 6.2% to about ₹7,823–7,828 cr, a little below estimates; revenue +10.7% to ₹49,244 cr. Guidance was cut from 1.5–3%; margin band kept at 20–22%. The CEO called it a soft quarter. ₹26 dividend, record date 3 Nov.
news.why: A guidance cut usually weighs on Infosys and IT peers; the US-listed shares were about 6% lower before the US open Friday.

news.headline: Kotak Bank Q2 profit up 26% to ₹5,645 cr; bad loans fall
news.summary: Standalone profit rose 29% to ₹4,212 cr, NII +16%, loans +25% and gross NPA fell to 1.04%. Margin narrowed to 4.31% from 4.53% in Q1 due to FCNR deposits.
news.why: First reaction today; strong profit and asset quality can support Bank Nifty, while the margin dip is the bear point.

news.headline: Nifty falls a fourth day to 22,600; midcaps −2.2%, smallcaps −2.9%
news.summary: Sensex fell 125.56 points to 73,123.83 and Nifty 87.65 points; all sectors ended lower, led by metal, consumer durables and realty. India VIX rose 6.3% to 16.76.
news.why: Heavy selling in mid and small caps shows risk appetite is weak; short trades need tight stop-losses.

news.headline: FIIs buy ₹888 cr, DIIs ₹3,235 cr on Friday
news.summary: Foreign investors were small net buyers after Thursday's ₹3,459 cr sale; domestic funds bought for a fourth day.
news.why: Steady DII buying is cushioning falls, but FIIs remain net sellers over the week.

news.headline: Wall Street ends lower on oil: Dow −1.2%, S&P −0.5%
news.summary: The Dow fell to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq to 25,955.34. The US 10-year yield rose to 4.99%.
news.why: A soft global lead adds to caution; Nasdaq futures were up 0.66% early Monday, a small offset.

news.headline: Nikkei opens 0.9% lower, Kospi slips; chip makers weak
news.summary: Nikkei opened at 62,129 and Kospi at 5,538.83. Doubts over AI-spending returns weigh on chips before SK hynix and Samsung results on 28–29 Oct.
news.why: Mildly weak Asia supports a cautious start in India.

news.headline: Fed, BoJ and ECB decide this week; Fed hold ~90% priced, December hike ~79%
news.summary: Markets expect all three to hold. Oil-driven inflation fears keep a December Fed hike likely. The Fed statement comes late Wednesday IST.
news.why: A hold is priced in; any hawkish hint would lift the dollar and yields, hurting FII flows, IT and gold.

news.headline: Jio Platforms IPO subscribed 22.19x; allotment today, listing 28 Oct
news.summary: QIBs bid 70.55x, NIIs 14x and retail 2.72x. Refunds are due Tuesday and listing is expected Wednesday 28 Oct. About ₹27,500 cr of fresh money will repay Reliance Jio Infocomm debt.
news.why: Strong demand supports Reliance sentiment; refunds release cash back to investors from Tuesday.

news.headline: IDFC First profit nearly triples; AU SFB up 53%
news.summary: IDFC First's standalone profit rose to ₹1,044.6 cr from ₹352 cr, with gross NPA down to 1.32%. AU Small Finance Bank's profit rose 53% to ₹858 cr.
news.why: Weekend results get their first reaction today; mid-sized private banks could outperform.

news.headline: JSW Steel profit more than triples; Adani Power +134%; Tata Motors back in profit
news.summary: JSW Steel profit rose to ₹5,279 cr (revenue +20.7%), Adani Power to ₹6,919 cr, CG Power +43.7% to ₹412 cr. Tata Motors' consolidated revenue rose 36% and it swung to a ₹1,257 cr profit.
news.why: Strong numbers after a heavy sell-off in metals can trigger a bounce, though oil and global risk may cap it.

news.headline: Coforge profit up 56%; raises FY27 margin guidance to 16%
news.summary: Revenue rose 53.6% to ₹6,170.8 cr and PAT 56.5% to ₹588 cr. Order intake was $1.04 bn with eight large deals; the CEO expects 17% margin next year.
news.why: A bright spot in IT against Infosys's guidance cut; mid-tier IT may outperform large caps.

news.headline: Dr Reddy's Q2 profit falls 31–36% on lower US lenalidomide sales
news.summary: Net profit fell to about ₹925 cr. The company linked the weakness mainly to lower lenalidomide revenue in North America. Reports differ on the exact percentage.
news.why: Likely to pressure the stock and the pharma index today.

news.headline: BPCL profit falls 21% to ₹4,863 cr; refining margin jumps to $32.53
news.summary: Revenue rose about 30%, but marketing margins were squeezed by costly crude. Board approved a subsidiary for a 10 mn tonne Andhra Pradesh refinery. Stock closed −1.74% at ₹281.95 before the results.
news.why: Strong refining offsets weak fuel retail; $115 oil remains the risk for all oil marketing companies.

news.headline: Gold slips below $4,000 after worst week in over four months
news.summary: Spot gold was near $3,995. Oil-led inflation fears revived Fed-hike bets and fund selling added pressure; MCX December gold ended near ₹1,42,734 on Friday.
news.why: Gold ETFs such as GOLDBEES may stay soft; a weaker rupee only partly cushions them.

news.headline: Rupee weakens to about 94.93–95 per dollar
news.summary: The rupee fell 12 paise to 94.93 (provisional) on Friday as oil rose; Goodreturns' ticker shows ₹95.01. The record low is 96.96.
news.why: A weaker rupee raises import costs and can prompt FII selling; it helps IT and pharma exporters' rupee earnings.

gold.label: Weak, just under $4,000
gold.summary: World gold was near $3,995 early Monday after a ~4% weekly fall, its worst in over four months, as $115 oil revived Fed-hike bets; MCX December gold ended Friday near ₹1,42,734 per 10g (−0.4%). Gold ETFs like GOLDBEES may stay soft; a rupee near 95 gives only a small cushion. Expect roughly ₹1,40,000–1,44,600 until the Fed decision late Wednesday IST; an actual Iran strike is the main upside risk.
gold.how: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic gold rate: world gold in dollars × USD/INR, plus import duty. So both world events and the rupee move them.

scenarios.title: Dollar slides again
scenarios.why: The dollar index rose to 102 and the US 10-year yield to 5.14% on Monday, which pushed gold below $4,150. A renewed slide would lift world gold; a firmer rupee would trim part of the gain for Indian ETFs.
scenarios.line: Dollar firm and yields near 5%; a slide would help gold.

scenarios.title: Fed holds on 28 Oct (~91% odds)
scenarios.why: Markets price about 90.6% odds of no change this week. A calm statement keeps yields and the dollar steady and could let gold steady above $4,000; a firmer rupee would trim part of any gain in India.
scenarios.line: A hold is priced in; a December hike (~79% odds) is what caps gold.

scenarios.title: Fed hikes on 28 Oct (small odds)
scenarios.why: A surprise hike would lift the dollar and yields and push gold lower; FII selling in India would likely weaken the rupee and cushion part of the fall.
scenarios.line: Unlikely now; gold could drop toward $3,900 if it happens.

scenarios.title: Gulf conflict widens, oil spikes
scenarios.why: Gold usually jumps on war fears, and higher oil weakens the rupee, so Indian gold ETFs gain on both counts. The catch: costly oil also feeds inflation and Fed-hike fears, which has capped gold's rallies recently, so gains can fade.
scenarios.when: 25–26 Oct: Houthi missiles at Riyadh; Trump says a strike is 'a possibility'; Brent $116.72 Fri
scenarios.line: Oil at a six-month high; gold rises on an actual strike, but hike fears have capped rallies.

scenarios.title: US–Iran de-escalation
scenarios.why: Less war risk removes some safe-haven buying, though cheaper oil also lowers inflation and hike fears, which helps gold. The clearer effect for India is a stronger rupee, which pulls the rupee price of gold down.
scenarios.when: 26 Oct: Trump floats a deal; Iran says contacts continue through intermediaries
scenarios.line: Less haven demand and a stronger rupee pull Indian gold down.

scenarios.title: Rupee slides past 97
scenarios.why: Every 1% fall in the rupee adds roughly 1% to Indian gold ETF prices even if world gold is flat. Brent above $115 and FII selling are pushing the rupee toward 95.
scenarios.when: USD/INR ~94.93–95.01 on 23–26 Oct vs record low 96.96
scenarios.line: Rupee near 95; each 1% fall adds ~1% to gold ETFs, even with gold flat.

scenarios.title: Rupee recovers
scenarios.why: The mid-October rupee rally has faded as oil rose. A renewed recovery, for example on Jio IPO inflows or a trade deal, would keep pressure on Indian gold ETFs.
scenarios.when: Rupee fell two days in a row to ~94.93 on 23 Oct
scenarios.line: Rally has faded; each 1% rupee gain cuts ~1% off gold ETFs.

scenarios.title: Stock market sell-off
scenarios.why: Investors move money into gold when stocks fall. The WGC says weak Indian equities drove gold ETF buying in September. In a severe crash gold can dip briefly as people sell everything to raise cash, then recover.
scenarios.line: Mid and small caps fell ~2–3% Fri; deeper falls can push money to gold.

scenarios.title: Central banks keep buying
scenarios.why: China's central bank added 21 tonnes in September, its 23rd straight monthly purchase. Steady official buying tends to limit how far gold falls, though it rarely drives short-term moves.
scenarios.line: China added 21 t in Sept (23rd month); limits downside.

scenarios.title: India cuts import duty
scenarios.why: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic price, which includes customs duty. A duty cut would lower the Indian gold price, and ETF prices, overnight by about the size of the cut, as happened in the July 2024 Budget. A duty hike would do the opposite.
scenarios.line: Domestic gold, and ETFs, drop overnight by about the cut.

items.name: Dr Reddy's Laboratories
items.head: Q2 profit falls 31–36% to about ₹925 cr
items.detail: Lower lenalidomide (Revlimid generic) sales in North America hit earnings; reports differ on the exact percentage.

items.head: Q2 profit −62% to ₹154 cr despite revenue +161%
items.detail: Revenue jumped to ₹1,935 cr but profit fell from ₹405 cr; realty was among the worst sectors Friday (−2.38%).

items.name: Shree Cement
items.head: Q2 profit −15% to ₹262 cr; revenue +24%
items.detail: Higher costs offset strong sales growth.

items.name: Adani Energy Solutions
items.head: Q2 profit more than doubles to ₹1,322.85 cr; revenue +52.7% to ₹10,075.54 cr
items.detail: Profit also rose 15.1% from Q1. Big growth in transmission and smart-meter work. Results came after the close, so today is the first reaction.
items.holdNote: Not yet priced in; Adani group shares fell Friday, so use a stop-loss.

items.name: Havells India
items.head: Q2 revenue +35% to ₹6,417 cr; profit +11% to ₹353 cr
items.detail: Very strong sales growth, but profit grew far slower, so margins thinned. The market may focus on margins on the earnings call.
items.holdNote: First reaction today; margin squeeze is the risk that can turn the move negative.

items.name: Indian Hotels (IHCL)
items.head: Q2 profit +22.6% to ₹350 cr; revenue +21.7%; FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 15–17%
items.detail: Raising full-year guidance mid-year signals strong demand into the wedding and holiday season.
items.holdNote: Already rose about 4% on Thursday; wait for a dip rather than chase. Guidance raise supports the 2–4 week view.

items.detail: Takes FY27 order inflows past ₹22,000 cr. The new orders are about 9% of FY26 revenue of ₹27,143 cr: useful, not transformational. Clients not named.

items.detail: A charter adds steady revenue over its term; duration not stated. Size versus yearly revenue not confirmed.

guide._all: Each card is a company-specific event from the latest filings and news. Green = likely to support the share, red = likely to pressure it, amber = watch. Friday-evening and Saturday results (Infosys, Kotak, IDFC First, AU SFB, Coforge, JSW Steel, Tata Motors, BPCL, Dr Reddy's) get their first reaction today. Shriram Finance and IndusInd fell on Friday despite better profits, so they are amber. No client-loss or order-cancellation news found since the last update. Review-by dates are counted in trading days (10 Nov is a market holiday).
guide.Can rise: Positive triggers. A share does not always rise on good news, especially if it ran up before the announcement or the overall market is weak.
guide.Can fall: Negative triggers. Results misses, big investor exits and weak business updates usually hit the share on the day and can weigh for weeks.
guide.Order won: An order matters most when it is big compared with the company's yearly revenue (5–10% or more is significant for smaller companies). Repeat orders and orders in a new area are good signs of future growth. Check the execution period: a 24-month order adds revenue slowly. Being named the only qualified bidder (Goodluck) is a step before an order, not an order itself.
guide.Results: Shares react to results versus expectations, not just growth. Profit growing slower than sales signals squeezed margins, in-line results after a run-up often get sold (Nestle), and guidance for the next quarter can matter more than the quarter itself (Wipro). The earnings call commentary often matters as much as the numbers.
guide.Business update: Monthly sales, pre-sales and festive data give an early read on the quarter before results come out.
guide.Board decision: Board outcomes that usually lift a share: buyback, bonus, stock split, special dividend, demerger or merger that simplifies the group. Ones that can pressure it: big equity fund raise (QIP or rights issue) that adds new shares, large acquisitions that need fresh capital (Aegis), or large related-party deals.
guide.Stake sale: When a promoter or big investor sells in a block deal, the share often falls on the day because the sale is at a discount. If quality institutions buy, it usually recovers within weeks.
guide.Regulatory: For pharma: a USFDA warning letter or import alert is a big negative, while a Form 483 with a few procedural observations (Dr Reddy's) is usually minor. Approvals, certifications and cuts in tax demands (Paytm) are positives; new or higher tax demands (Mphasis) and lawsuits (Bank of Baroda) are negatives, though most are disputed for years. Rule changes by NPCI, SEBI or the exchanges (UPI fees, F&O exits) can move a whole group of stocks.
guide.Management change: A sudden exit of a CEO or CFO can spook investors; a planned succession usually doesn't.
guide.Corporate action: Takeovers, open offers and delisting plans. These change who owns the company and can create short-term price moves. If the share already trades above the deal price (IDBI Bank), the upside depends on the open-offer terms.
guide.Fund raise: Debt or government loans don't dilute shareholders. Equity raises (QIP, rights, preferential issue) add new shares and can weigh on the price.
guide.Legal claim: A lawsuit or legal claim against a company. A big headline number can hit the share for days, but most claims take years and are often dismissed or settled for far less. Watch whether the court admits the case and what the company files.

items.title: US midterm elections and Iran risk
items.latest: 25–26 Oct: Trump said there would be no strike on Iran on Sunday, then said 'there's a possibility I will' while also floating a deal; Iran says contacts continue through intermediaries. Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh and southern Saudi Arabia on 25 Oct. Brent settled at $116.72 Friday. Earlier (22 Oct) NYT reported US–Israel strike plans for after the 3 Nov midterms.
items.effect: After 3 Nov the Iran pledge expires, so oil and safe-haven risk could rise. Higher oil hurts India (rupee, inflation, oil marketing companies, paints, airlines) and helps gold and upstream oil.
items.watch: Any US/Israeli action before or after 3 Nov, Hormuz shipping, Israel's 27 Oct election, Brent above $116

items.title: India–US trade deal
items.who: Commerce Ministry and US Trade Representative
items.latest: 22 Oct: EAM Jaishankar said the India–US trade deal is in the 'last mile', after Trump called it 'pretty close' and Rubio said it should come in 'weeks, not months'. The US rate on most Indian goods is 18% under the February framework. No signing announced as of 26 Oct.
items.effect: A deal that lowers US tariffs would help exporters that depend on the US: textiles and apparel, gems and jewellery, auto parts, chemicals, seafood. Failure or new tariffs would hit the same group.
items.when: Announcement 'within weeks' per Rubio; leaders' signing could follow
items.likely: Medium to high: both sides say it is close, but nothing signed
items.watch: Any announcement during Rubio's visit; tariff rates for textiles, gems, auto parts, chemicals

items.title: US Federal Reserve rate decision
items.latest: 26 Oct: CME FedWatch prices about 90.6% odds of a hold this week and about 79.4% odds of a hike in December, as $115 oil revives inflation fears. The US 10-year yield is about 5.0%. The BoJ and ECB also meet this week and are expected to hold.
items.effect: A hold is mildly positive for Indian stocks, the rupee and gold. A surprise hike would lift the dollar and US yields, push FIIs to sell more, and hurt IT and gold.
items.watch: Statement tone on oil-led inflation; December hike hints; US core PCE later this week

items.title: RBI rate decision: another hike likely in December
items.latest: 21 Oct: Minutes of the 5–7 Oct meeting show all six members voted for the 25 bps hike to 5.50%; Governor Malhotra said rate cuts are off the table and the next move is a hike or pause. CPI is forecast at 6.0% in Oct–Dec and 5.7% in Jan–Mar; FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7.1%. Two members (Nagesh Kumar, Ram Singh) preferred a neutral stance.
items.effect: A hike raises borrowing costs: negative for rate-sensitive stocks such as NBFCs, real estate and autos, and for bond prices. Banks can gain on margins at first. A pause would be a relief rally trigger.
items.likely: High for another 25 bps hike if October CPI stays near 6%
items.watch: October CPI (12 Nov), liquidity operations, rupee and crude

items.title: Possible Trump–Xi–Putin meeting at APEC in Shenzhen
items.latest: 22 Oct: All three leaders are expected at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Putin called a three-way meeting 'certainly possible'; Trump backed it but wants the focus on denuclearisation, which Xi resists. The Kremlin said nothing is agreed.
items.effect: A meeting that eases US–China or Russia tensions would help global risk appetite and FII flows into emerging markets; a public falling-out would do the reverse. Oil could ease if it touches on Iran.
items.when: APEC summit; exact date not confirmed in sources checked
items.likely: Low to medium: discussed, but no agenda agreed
items.watch: Confirmation of a meeting; any US–China tariff or chip-export announcement

items.title: US waives sanctions on Russian energy exports
items.latest: Around 18 Oct Trump waived Graham Act sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy exports. On 21 Oct the Kremlin said Putin agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, and a US official said Russia accepted a trilateral meeting.
items.effect: More Russian oil on the market eases crude prices and lowers the risk of US penalties on Indian refiners that buy Russian crude: positive for oil marketing companies, airlines, paints and the rupee.
items.likely: Done; Congress critics could push back
items.watch: Whether the waiver lasts and Brent's reaction to Hormuz news

items.title: OPEC+ oil output for December
items.latest: On 4–5 Oct OPEC+ kept November output unchanged. The next monthly decision (for December) is due in early November.
items.effect: Higher output would ease crude and help India's rupee, inflation and oil marketing companies. A cut would do the opposite.
items.watch: Brent at $116.72 (23 Oct settle), a six-month high; any extra supply would ease it

items.title: IDBI Bank sold to Fairfax (60.72% stake at ₹81/share)
items.latest: On 14 Oct the Cabinet approved Fairfax's ₹52,878 cr bid: the government sells 30.48% and LIC 30.24% at ₹81 a share. IDBI jumped 9% to ₹90.39 on 14 Oct, then fell 8.1% to ₹83.07 on 15 Oct. Fairfax reportedly plans to combine IDBI Bank, Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital into one group. On 16 Oct Business Standard reported Fairfax proposes contributing Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital to IDBI Bank; CSB Bank denied merger talks with IDBI. On 17–19 Oct IDBI reported Q2 profit down 39% to ₹2,205 cr (the year-ago figure had a one-off ₹1,699 cr NSDL gain).
items.effect: Largest privatisation since Air India and a boost to reform sentiment. For IDBI shareholders, the stock already trades above ₹81; open-offer terms for public shareholders are not yet announced, so chasing the jump is risky. Fairfax must merge or exit CSB Bank, where it owns 40%.
items.likely: High (approved); RBI fit-and-proper and CCI clearances still needed
items.watch: Open-offer price and size; RBI approval; government's plan to sell its remaining 15%

items.title: Scrap LTCG tax on shares (and possibly cut STT)
items.who: Proposed by SBI Research · Decision: Finance Ministry
items.latest: SBI Research (12 Oct) proposed scrapping long-term capital gains tax on equities, with a 2–3 year holding period, to stem FPI outflows of ₹3.04 lakh cr this year. On 14 Oct the Finance Minister said it is 'too early to comment' and announced no change. On 19 Oct, Bernstein said an LTCG cut alone won't bring back FPIs and cut its Nifty target to 25,000.
items.effect: If done, a big positive for the whole market and for FPI flows; brokers, exchanges and AMCs would gain most. Current LTCG is 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh. A cut in STT on F&O (raised to 0.05% on futures in April) would mainly help brokers and BSE.
items.likely: Low to medium: equity LTCG brought in about ₹1.29 lakh cr, hard to give up with a ~4.5% fiscal deficit
items.watch: Pre-Budget consultations (Nov–Jan) and any Finance Ministry comment

items.title: SEBI closing auction for the final price
items.latest: SEBI finalised the rules on 15 Oct: a 10-minute closing auction from 3:30 to 3:40 PM on all trading days, index and stock derivatives trading until 3:45 PM (some expiring index contracts excepted), and expiring derivatives settled on the volume-weighted average price of the last 30 minutes.
items.effect: Changes how the closing price is set. Mainly affects traders, index funds and exchanges; little effect on long-term holders. BSE was among today's top Nifty losers (−1.8%).
items.when: Most changes from 7 Dec 2026; limit/iceberg orders into the auction from 8 Feb 2027
items.watch: Exchange circulars and broker system changes

items.title: 0.4% UPI merchant fee on payments above ₹2,000
items.latest: On 13 Oct NPCI deferred the 0.4% merchant discount rate on certain UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 until after Diwali; a new date will be notified.
items.effect: A fee on large UPI merchant payments would give payment companies a revenue source; small merchants would bear the cost. Positive for payment firms such as Paytm when it starts.
items.when: After Diwali (8 Nov); new date to be notified
items.watch: NPCI circular with the start date

items.title: More PSU stake sales (OFS) this year
items.latest: About ₹55,757 cr raised so far in FY27 from stake sales in 9 PSUs (including LIC and Coal India). With IDBI, receipts cross the ₹80,000 cr target for the first time in 8 years. The government may sell its residual IDBI stake in the market.
items.effect: An offer-for-sale (OFS) is usually priced at a discount, so the PSU stock often dips for a few days around the sale. Meeting the target can reduce pressure for further big sales this year.
items.when: Through March 2027; OFS dates are announced a day ahead
items.watch: OFS announcements on NSE/BSE (usually the evening before)

items.title: Union Budget 2027
items.latest: Preparations are under way. The LTCG/STT debate, disinvestment, capex and the fiscal deficit (~4.5% of GDP) will be the key themes.
items.effect: Tax changes on capital gains or STT, customs duty on gold, and capex plans can move whole sectors on the day.
items.watch: Pre-Budget meetings and leaks from December
